profile.headline: Software Developer at IBM 👩🏻‍💻| AI Engineering • Backend Systems • DevOps & Automation
profile.summary:
Andrea Ovalle-Flores is a Software Developer at IBM focused on building scalable systems across AI, backend development, and DevOps.

Her work sits at the intersection of automation and compliance, where she develops internal systems that support audit processes and improve operational efficiency across engineering teams. This includes building and integrating solutions using AI (including retrieval-augmented generation), designing backend services, and developing CI/CD pipelines to streamline workflows.

She has primarily worked within compliance-focused environments, contributing to systems aligned with frameworks such as SOC 2. This experience has shaped her approach to building software that not only scales, but also meets real-world security and audit requirements.

Andrea holds a Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity from The University of Texas at San Antonio, and brings that foundation into her work building secure and reliable systems.

At her core, she enjoys building — whether that’s developing new systems, improving existing workflows, or exploring emerging tools.

She is currently expanding her skill set across cloud platforms and modern AI tooling while continuing to focus on creating practical, high-impact solutions

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
- Design and develop internal systems that support audit and compliance workflows, improving efficiency and scalability across engineering and security teams.

- Contributed to the re-architecture and replatforming of Auditree, a compliance automation tool that aggregates data from multiple cloud and security endpoints (AWS, IBM Cloud, Azure) to generate audit-ready reports on control status.

- Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines using tools such as Tekton and Jenkins to automate data collection, validation, and reporting processes.

- Develop backend services and scripts (primarily in Python and Bash) to process logs, integrate APIs/webhooks, and streamline system-to-system communication.

- Implement AI-driven solutions, including a RAG-based chatbot leveraging vector databases (Qdrant) and frameworks such as LangChain/LangGraph, deployed on ROSA clusters to support intelligent data retrieval.

- Contribute to emerging initiatives using AI for audit evidence review and cross-framework control mapping, helping automate traditionally manual compliance processes.

- Work with containerized environments (Podman) and in-memory data stores (Redis) to support scalable and performant system design.

- Assist in building and evolving a SOC 2 data infrastructure, including efforts to design a centralized source-of-truth database (AWS RDS PostgreSQL) to track audit metrics and enable workflow automation.

- Utilize infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform (foundational exposure) to support environment setup and configuration.

- Collaborate in Agile environments, contributing to sprint planning, standups, and delivery tracking; helped design and manage team workflows and project boards using Monday.com.

- Participate in AI experimentation and prototyping, including work with IBM WatsonX Orchestrate and MCP-based tooling to explore automation and developer productivity enhancements.

positions.title: Java Tutor
positions.description: Tutored college students taking Java I courses at the University of Texas at San Antonio where understanding of the programming language, analytical skills, communication skills, and problem-solving skills was used to help struggling students

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Fellow
positions.description:
We examined a critical issue faced by the global economy – disruptive shortage in the semi-conductor industry.

 The study identified various disruption points in supply chains and proposes a set of short-term and long-term remedial strategies to mitigate the shortage and potential risks in the future. This research was used to provide useful insights to better coordinate the partners in the semiconductor industry for a more resilient chip manufacturing environment

positions.title: IBM Accelerate Participant | Client Engineering and Technical Sales Track
positions.description:
IBM Accelerate is an eight-week program during the summer of 2022. The program identified and equipped me with the knowledge and readiness I need to be prepared for future consideration of opportunities within the technology industry.

I was placed on the Client and Technical Sales track where I learned about IBM's technology sales. Through this program, I have connected with many and learned a lot of foundational skills needed in the workplace. 

As part of this program, I was placed on a team to engineer a chatbot using IBM's Watson AI Assistant that will improve staff satisfaction, decrease wait times of a customer, used AI running applications, brain-stormed the design of the chatbot, and engineered the chatbot together

positions.title: Excel with Dell Mentor Program Participant
positions.description:
This was a full Spring Semester mentorship program designed to help students develop and reach their
goals. I connected with many Dell workers and enjoyed meeting a lot of people. I also developed professionally by learning how to properly communicate, present, and work with others. Truly a fun program that has left me with many lessons to carry on forward in my career.
I also received a certificate for completing the program.

projects.title: Security Vulnerabilities in Quantum Operating Systems
projects.description:
This Security Brief was my Operating Systems Security final course project. It may be inaccurate as I had only 2 weeks to complete this. Feel free to provide constructive feedback because I am always open to learning something new. The reason I am posting this report is because I was genuinely proud of my work and the time I took to do research into complex research papers. In doing so, I learned A LOT about Quantum Computers. 
It took me a lot of courage to post this because of how complex Quantum Computer's work and how I did hard-core research into this for about 2 weeks. However, my Professor did encourage me to get this out there for the couple few to see. So again, feel free to provide feedback on what can be fixed. This report might even be edited and updated as I continue exploring quantum operating systems on my free time.
With that said, this report talks about the possibility of having a Quantum-based Operating System and its current flaws discovered in current research papers. I provide answers and information in Leyman-terms for everyone to see as well as citations to where I found my information.
